title: Cycle Capacity Risk Ledger and Floating Task Pool playbook
creator: Evan Brooks
description:
Problem: As we scale multiple initiatives (Dedicated, Private, Optimize), PMs frequently overcommit features into a cycle without a structured way to quantify capacity risk. This leads to mid-cycle scope churn, unplanned carryover, and uneven staffing pressure across teams.

Goal: Produce an operational playbook and lightweight tooling patterns that (1) quantify cycle-level capacity risk per initiative, (2) create a floating task pool for safe de-scope decisions, and (3) give clear decision rules for staff rebalancing and emergency surge. The deliverable should be a repeatable process, templates, and a one-page scoring ledger to use in planning review.

Scope: This ticket covers the playbook creation, a spreadsheet template (capacity-risk ledger), planning meeting script, and a pilot run across two initiatives in the next cycle. It does NOT include automation/integration with JIRA/Linear (follow-up ticket).

Proposed approach:
- Define a simple capacity-risk scoring rubric (effort, cross-team dependencies, infra uncertainty, customer SLA impact, release coupling). Each axis 1-5.
- Weight axes to create a single Cycle Risk score and map to bands: Green (<10), Amber (10-16), Red (>16).
- Create 'Floating Task Pool' rules: max 12% of cycle capacity (configurable), tasks eligible for floating pool must be shippable-deferred items with <3 dependencies and non-high-security scope.
- Design planning meeting flow: 30m pre-triage, 60m planning review, 15m final decision cadence. Use ledger during review to prioritize and assign floating slate.
- Pilot: run with Growth L10 initiative and Console Observability initiative for cycle 2026-W10; track decisions and outcomes.

Acceptance criteria:
- A one-page ledger template (Google Sheet) with scoring fields and auto-calculated risk band exists and is linked in the playbook.
- Playbook (Confluence doc) includes meeting script, decision rules, and FAQ.
- Pilot run completed with two initiatives; retrospective notes captured and three measurable improvements defined (e.g., fewer mid-cycle scope changes, improved on-time delivery).
- PMs and Eng leads sign-off on rules and floating pool sizing for next two cycles.

Metrics to track in pilot:
- Mid-cycle scope change rate (baseline -> pilot)
- Percentage of tasks moved into floating pool vs. carried over
- On-time delivery rate for scoped items
- Staff load variance (standard deviation of weekly allocation across teams)

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Primary: Priya Rao (PM lead), Marco Chen (Eng lead - Runtime), Lena Ortiz (Design), Rahul Iyer (Prod Ops)
